h: Moshe’s Vision Illuminates Israel’s Portion in Torah

p: "Let me cross over, please, and see
אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה וְגוֹ׳ (דְּבָרִים ג, כה)
so why did he mention seeing?
"Go up to the top of the summit
and lift up your eyes," etc.,
for you shall not cross," etc.;
since He said "lift up your eyes,"
it is certainly to see with his eyes;
so why did He say further,
"and he shall cause them to inherit
the land which you will see";
as in the work of Creation,
where it is written on each day:
"And God saw that it was good"
that is, through His seeing, may His Name be blessed,
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, instilled
in the great ones of Yisrael as well,
those of Yisrael worthy of it
also merited the power of seeing
(and it was explained in Parashas Masei).
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ (דְּבָרִים ג, כד)
And this is what it says in this parsha (Devarim 3:24):
it should have said "to Your servant,"
Yisrael merited the power of seeing.
meaning the light "that it is good";
I will bring the light "that it is good"
the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
that is, that the light be
that one would say of it
only at the splitting of the Sea
and at the giving of the Torah,
nevertheless, since it will be engraved in the heart,
עַל וְכָל זֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שׁוֶֹה לִי
on "Yet all this is worth nothing to me":
for whatever is engraved in the heart,
through his seeing in the land.
"Go up to the top of the summit
and lift up your eyes," etc.,
the light "that it is good" into Eretz Yisrael.
כִּי לֹא תַעֲבוֹר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן וְגוֹ׳
"For you shall not cross this Jordan," etc.;
"and he shall cause them to inherit
the land which you will see":
that is, in Torah she'b'al peh;
as is written in the holy Zohar
"and he gave it to the kohanim, the sons of Levi."
for it is the arrangement of Eretz Yisrael";
for Yehoshua gave them the land as inheritance
and apportioned to each one his portion
"and he — Hu — shall cause them to inherit";
as is written (Idra Zuta, Zohar III 290a):
And it likewise denotes the Yovel,
who merits the light of Torah she'b'al peh
and knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul";
which is the joining of Chochmah and Binah,
"and knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul";
hidden away for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh.
And there are those who merit
as they will merit the light in the future,
which will be at the end of the sixth millennium,
And both are through the attribute of Yosef,
through which is the drawing down
to the aspect of Knesses Yisrael.
And Yehoshua, who is of his seed,
is the one who apportions and bequeaths

As Rabbi Simlai taught: A person should always set forth praise of God and only then pray for his own needs. From where do we derive this? We derive it …”
